plan: Second-price sealed-bid auctions make truthful bidding a dominant strategy. With iid uniform values and no informative history, shading down risks missing positive-profit wins; shading up risks winning at a price above value if outbid only slightly. Maximizing long-run profit means bidding exactly my value each round. With value 42, I bid 42; ties at 42 split win probability with zero or positive expected profit. Execute: bid 42.

In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ bids. There is no prior-round history to exploit in round 1 of 1. With value $29 drawn uniformly from $0–$49, I should bid 29 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 29, paying that amount, ensuring non-negative profit.

[ True second‑price auctions make bidding your true value a dominant strategy: your bid only affects whether you win, not the price you pay (which equals the second-highest bid). With no exploitable history and one round, shading risks losing profitable wins without reducing price. Therefore, bid exactly my private value ($48) to maximize expected profit. If I win, expected profit is 48 minus the second-highest bid; if I lose, profit is 0. ]
